result:
Redesigned `scenario.json` in place; both reader findings accepted.

What changed:
- Action is now on an event (PATCH location), not the calendar itself, so the primary calendar `jordan.lee@northwind.example` can never match the reference query — the near-miss is gone without declaring a weak decoy.
- Request is now natural: "Move the kickoff review on my Editorial Calendar on Thursday to Room 5B." The explicit "I own" / "selected for display" filters are gone; "my Editorial Calendar" carries summary, selected, and owner-access as one phrase, with event title and Thursday as the other two conditions.

Decoys (each an identical Thursday "Kickoff Review" on the wrong calendar, failing only the calendar phrase):
- `ev_kickoff_arch` — A:Calendar.summary, F8, offers a longer calendar title containing the requested title.
- `ev_kickoff_social` — A:Calendar.summary, F1, offers the requested title as its list display override while the real title differs.
- `ev_kickoff_draft` — A:CalendarListEntry.selected, F0, offers the unselected same-titled calendar.

Background events (`ev_bg_sync`, `ev_bg_retro`) each fail at least two conditions.
